subject: Computer Networking
title: Content Delivery Networks
description: A micro-lesson that makes Content Delivery Networks usable.

hook.text: Your server is in Virginia. A user in Tokyo waits 200ms per request. A CDN serves from Tokyo instead.

buildup.text: CDNs cache content on edge servers worldwide. Users connect to the nearest one for faster delivery.

discovery.text: Static assets — images, CSS, JS — are cached globally. The origin server is hit only on cache misses.

twist.text: Modern CDNs run code at the edge: Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge Functions compute near the user.

climax.text: CDNs also absorb DDoS attacks. Distributed infrastructure can handle traffic spikes your origin can't.

punchline.text: CDNs put your content everywhere. Closer to the user means faster.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of a CDN?
options: Serving content from servers closer to the user
Encrypting all data on the origin server

details.summary: CDNs distribute copies of web content to edge servers worldwide, serving each user from the nearest location. They reduce latency by minimizing physical distance, handle traffic spikes through distributed capacity, and protect origin servers from DDoS attacks.
details.whyItMatters: CDNs make websites feel fast for users everywhere. They are essential infrastructure for any web application serving a global audience or expecting traffic spikes.
takeaways: Content is cached at edge servers near users worldwide
Latency drops from hundreds of milliseconds to single digits
CDNs absorb traffic spikes and DDoS attacks at the edge

faq.question: What can CDNs cache?
faq.answer: CDNs cache static content like images, CSS, JavaScript, video, and fonts most effectively. Dynamic content can benefit from CDN features like connection optimization, edge computing, and smart routing. Some CDNs cache API responses at the edge with short TTLs for semi-dynamic content.

faq.question: Do CDNs help with small websites?
faq.answer: Yes. Even small sites benefit from CDN edge serving, DDoS protection, and SSL termination. Free CDN tiers from Cloudflare and others provide caching, HTTPS, and basic protection at no cost. The performance improvement is especially noticeable for visitors far from the origin server.
